statement: an ops directory that EXISTS but cannot be LISTED refuses the load (OpLogStore.verifyOpsDirectoryListable) — it used to read as 'no log yet' through the presence-only glob and send Bootstrap minting FRESH paragraph ids: a second, parallel history over the writer's intact one

the sync-merge read throws on an unreadable file too, so a CLOSED document — DerivedManuscript, and through it MCP read_document, search-adjacent readers and the compile pipeline — never silently derives a shorter manuscript; the compile path's Source protocol is throwing, so an unreadable file FAILS the compile through the DurableProgress catch instead of emitting a book missing chapters
reachability: LIVE — MCP reads of closed docs; every compile

scope: segment checksum vs unreadable — the two failure kinds
statement: a READABLE-but-corrupt segment (checksum/magic/decompress failure) still salvages decompressable lines and records a quarantine skip — partial truth, recorded — while an UNREADABLE segment throws: nothing can be known about it, so nothing can be honestly salvaged. Two different answers to two genuinely different questions

deliberately lenient after RULING-54, each with its reason in place: the app-fringe readers (search content, background word-count stats, closed-doc task derivation, the rename pre-check, the statement-preview classifier, the scenes sidebar, the project task log) read via try? and SKIP an unreadable doc — every one of them meets the loud refusal the moment the doc is opened, and none can mutate anything from the shortened view.
